title: Mirendil's AI Agents Write 99% of Code to Pretrain Frontier Coding Model
summary:
The company has transitioned to post-training its first large-scale coding model after successfully substituting a full team of engineers with AI agents. These agents authored over 99% of the codebase and managed the research experiments, while 1 human researcher directed the strategy and decided which results to trust. Mirendil plans to release API access and independent evaluations shortly, and the project was completed without using knowledge distillation to reach its performance levels.

Mirendil-Base contains between 100B and 500B parameters and was developed from scratch in 3.5 months using less than $10M in compute. The organization is now scaling this approach to a "Large" variant with 500B to 2T parameters and an "XL" version targeting up to 10T parameters. The initiative aims to democratize frontier AI development by utilizing recursive self-improvement to drastically reduce the expertise and financial capital required to train foundation models.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Our first pretrained model was built by one researcher in 3.5 months, with less than $10M in compute
selectedTweets.text:
We formally announced Mirendil less than 4 months ago. Today, I'm excited to share an important milestone for:

Pretraining at scale without a pretraining team.

Mirendil's mission is to solve Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) and use it to democratize frontier AI development, ultimately accelerating science and technology. At Mirendil, when we think about RSI, we think holistically about the company as an intelligent entity that self-improves toward its goal. From that perspective, the most powerful notion of acceleration is reducing the time and resources (number of human experts, compute, and other costs) needed to achieve ambitious goals.

Given that pretraining is perhaps the most important yet most challenging part of frontier AI development, we decided to run an ambitious controlled experiment: Starting fully from scratch, can we significantly reduce the time, number of human experts, and compute resources needed to go all the way to successfully pretraining a strong coding model at scale?

Mirendil-Base is the result of this experiment. Our first pretrained model was built by one researcher in 3.5 months, with less than $10M in compute. This includes all the research and small-scale experiments it took to get there, as well as the final training run.

The recipe holds up as the models get bigger. For reference, Mirendil-Base is in the 100B-500B parameter range, Mirendil-Base-Large in the 500B-2T range, and Mirendil-Base-XL in the 2T-10T range.

We're beginning to see a world where a single researcher, empowered by AI, can take on work that once required an entire research organization. As these systems improve, the bottleneck shifts from the size of a team to the ambition and judgment of the people directing them. This has profound implications for who gets to build AI and, ultimately, who gets to push the frontiers of science and technology forward.

We’ll share independent evaluations, post-training benchmarks and API-access sooner than you think so stay tuned!

Today, we're sharing a major milestone in our mission to democratize frontier AI development:  

Pretraining at scale without a pretraining team.  

We set out to answer an ambitious question: Can we significantly reduce the time, human expertise, and compute needed to pretrain a competitive foundation model from scratch?  

The result is Mirendil-Base, our first pretrained coding model, built by one researcher in just 3.5 months with less than $10M in compute, including all research, experimentation, and the final training run.  

Our approach is already showing promising results as we scale to even larger models.  

This is an important step toward a future where a single researcher, empowered by AI, can accomplish what once required an entire research organization. As these capabilities improve, we believe frontier AI development can become accessible to far more people and teams.  

More to come soon, including independent evaluations, post-training benchmarks, and API access.

selectedTweets.text:
Two landmark releases today on recursive self-improvement! What a timeline 🚀

Mirendil (@mirendil) reports pretraining Mirendil-Base, a 100B–500B coding model, from scratch in 3.5 months with one researcher and under $10M of compute; small-scale experiments included. Agents wrote over 99% of the code and ran the experiments, while the researcher chose directions and decided which results to trust. Larger versions are already training. Impressive leverage for a single person.

https://t.co/W7tarKwYU0

Recursive (@Recursive_SI) released Flint, an open-weights 40B coding model for fast local use. They built it from scratch in under 4 months with their automated research system, the Eureka Machine. Great to see autoresearch ship an actual model people can run.

https://t.co/8fwuh15Uoy

The framing seems to differ a little. Mirendil is reducing the people, compute and time needed per model, with a human directing agents. Recursive's Eureka Machine aims to automate more of the research loop itself. Both start with coding models, on the view that better coding speeds up AI research.
